intro.title: Digitise Your Quality Inspection Process
paragraphs: Consistent quality is what keeps customers loyal and recalls away. Yet many plants still record inspections on paper or in spreadsheets: results arrive late, defects are spotted after a whole batch is packed, and nobody can say for sure which line or shift is causing the problem.

Our manufacturing quality inspection software moves the whole process onto tablets and phones. Inspectors fill in digital inspection forms built around your quality standards, attach photos of defects and submit results instantly. Those results flow into an approval workflow and a real-time QRI dashboard, so supervisors, QA managers and plant heads see quality performance as it happens, not days later.

The QRI Dashboard is configured to your products, parameters and approval levels, so it fits the way your plant already works. It suits soap, detergent, cosmetics, pharmaceutical, chemical, plastics, food, FMCG and engineering manufacturers. Need it connected to your ERP or production systems? See our <csd>custom software development</csd> or <contact>talk to us about your plant</contact>.

faqs.title: QRI Dashboard FAQs
faqs.subtitle: Quick answers about quality inspection software and the QRI Dashboard.

items.a: The QRI Dashboard is a real-time quality dashboard for manufacturers. It collects digital inspection results from the shop floor and shows the Quality Rating Index, defect rates and trends by line, shift, batch, SKU and inspector.

items.q: What is manufacturing quality inspection software?
items.a: It is software that lets manufacturers record, monitor, analyse and approve quality inspections digitally instead of on paper. It standardises checks, captures defects with photos, tracks batches and produces real-time reports.

items.q: What do QRI, QDI and DPMO mean?
items.a: QRI (Quality Rating Index) is an overall quality score for a line, batch or product. QDI (Quality Defect Index) weighs defects by severity. DPMO (Defects Per Million Opportunities) measures how often defects occur relative to every chance for one.

items.q: Can the software match our existing inspection process?
items.a: Yes. Inspection forms, parameters, tolerances, defect categories and approval levels are configured around your current process and quality standards, so your team does not have to change how it works.

items.q: Can inspectors use it on the shop floor?
items.a: Yes. Inspectors use tablets or phones to fill in inspections, scan batch labels and take defect photos, and the app can keep working when the network is weak, syncing once connected.

items.q: How much does quality inspection software cost?
items.a: Typical costs are $4,000 to $10,000 for a single plant, $10,000 to $25,000 for multi-line and multi-brand setups, and $25,000 or more for multi-plant enterprises. We share a fixed quote after a free consultation.
